asks: Keep Calgary-Currie's communities together with minimal change, respect municipal boundaries, and put the two new seats in Calgary and Edmonton.
Keep Calgary-Acadia intact as a community of interest rather than splitting it.
Draw homogeneous (non-hybrid) constituencies, avoid splitting communities and artificial boundaries, and keep rural farming seats manageable.
Keep the upper Bow Valley landscape (Banff-Kananaskis, including Canmore and Banff) together in one riding rather than dividing it.
Preserve Calgary-Varsity with its current boundaries and give Calgary more representation.
Give Calgary at least one more seat on its growing periphery and keep Calgary-Acadia as designed.
Give Airdrie two electoral districts drawn to the city's municipal limits, ending the split of west Airdrie into Airdrie-Cochrane.

quote: This means that considering Airdrie’s municipal population alone, two electoral divisions that are equally divided, with no rural components, would actually serve populations of approximately 50,000 people each right now
note: Rejection quote: 'The current divisions act is more of a grab bag or catchment area for surrounding rural zones, and this is really not appropriate.' (EB-220). Fallback in answer to Mr. Clark (EB-222): if numbers must be made up, add the 'small rural doughnut around Airdrie' served by the library, i.e. something like A1.

quote: it’s far more appropriate for us to have Airdrie electoral districts that don’t make a third of our residents feel like an afterthought. Our municipal issues should not be diluted by those of other major municipalities like Cochrane, who deserve effective representation in their own right.
note: Argues against Airdrie-Cochrane from Airdrie's side; asks nothing specific about whom Cochrane should be with.
Lethbridge-East and Lethbridge-West cited only as a model for two city-only Airdrie seats (rule 6).

asks: Keep municipalities and communities intact and avoid blending urban and rural ridings, endorsing the Airdrie presenter's principle.

note: Calgary-Klein resident endorses the previous Airdrie presenter's principle that municipalities be represented; no request of her own on how Airdrie is divided (rule 17).

asks: Keep Banff-Kananaskis boundaries as they are, except move all of Millarville into it from Highwood, and account for growth in Canmore and Springbank.
Continuation of Jim Ridley: put all of Millarville in Banff-Kananaskis and keep rural rangeland out of Calgary.
Consider where Mount Royal University students live and place the campus more fully inside one riding rather than at the edge of Calgary-Elbow.

note: Airdrie named only as a place some students live; no request.
Chestermere named only as a place students commute from; no request.
Cochrane named only as a place students commute from; no request.

asks: Recognize Mount Royal students as a community and perhaps place them in the Calgary-Currie district rather than with affluent Calgary-Elbow neighbourhoods.
Keep Calgary-Glenmore as a credible, connected riding aligned with municipal boundaries; no specific boundary change asked.
Redraw Calgary-Elbow to add Richmond-Knob Hill and all of Lakeview, remove Glamorgan and Lower Mount Royal, and account for Marda Loop growth.
Move toward one person one vote, with more ridings in the big cities.

note: Cochrane named only for its library and as a joke ('arch enemy'); no request about Cochrane's district.

asks: Keep Banff-Kananaskis largely unchanged, group like communities, consider growth, and if tweaks are needed remove Elbow Valley and bring in Stoney Nakoda lands.

quote: our issues are definitely different than people that live in Cochrane or Calgary, and I think it would be a disservice to both groups to lump them together or to mix them.
note: Banff-Kananaskis resident; also notes 'In the last redraw it used to be that Cochrane was in with Banff' and wants B-K kept as is. Rejects putting Cochrane back with the Bow Valley; asks nothing about where Cochrane should go.

asks: Keep inner-city Calgary communities and municipal boundaries together (no urban-rural blending) and give Calgary more ridings.
Keep distinct rural and urban districts rather than pie-shaped hybrids, preserve geography and community identity, and add the new seats in north Calgary and south Edmonton.

note: Red Deer-South named only as a place she has lived; her objection to pie-shaped urban-rural districts names no place (HYBRID-GENERAL).
Lethbridge-West named only as a place she has lived; general opposition to pie-shaped hybrids is not tied to Lethbridge (rule 1).

asks: Allocate one of the new seats to northeast Calgary, keep northeast Calgary communities together and away from Airdrie or Chestermere, and unite the east side of Deerfoot with Calgary-Bhullar-McCall.

quote: For example, annexing any northeast community with the neighbouring towns of Airdrie or Chestermere may not make any sense at all.
note: Rejects joining northeast Calgary communities to Airdrie, from Calgary's side; the minority's Airdrie-Calgary districts take north Calgary, so read as a rejection of the A2 kind of arrangement. No want about Airdrie itself.

quote: For example, annexing any northeast community with the neighbouring towns of Airdrie or Chestermere may not make any sense at all.
note: Rejects joining east Calgary communities with Chestermere, from Calgary's side. No want about Chestermere itself.

asks: Keep Calgary-Glenmore intact and city ridings within municipal boundaries, and add seats in north Calgary and south Edmonton.
Give urban ridings more weight (fewer electors per riding than rural ones), respect municipal boundaries, and if Calgary-Buffalo must shrink, cut south of 17th Avenue.

note: Red Deer named only in family history (parents married there; relatives moved to Calgary or Red Deer); no request.

asks: Keep Calgary-Glenmore's boundaries the same or similar and do not add areas from outside city limits.
